note.note:
Subjective:
- Presenting complaint and trigger/exposure:
  - New-onset headache starting mid-morning yesterday; no identified trigger or exposure.
- Symptom timeline and progression:
  - Began yesterday mid-morning, built up over a short period, described as intense and throbbing; current pain severity ~8/10.
  - No variation with time of day, position, bending, coughing, or sneezing.
- ENT symptoms:
  - Throat swelling/closure sensation: denied.
  - Voice change/hoarseness: denied.
  - Dysphagia/odynophagia: denied.
  - Drooling: denied.
  - Nasal/ocular symptoms: no eye pain, no visual disturbances, no photophobia reported.
  - Stridor/noisy breathing: denied.
  - Dyspnea: denied.
  - Distribution of swelling (lips/tongue/uvula/face): none reported.
  - Ear/neck symptoms: no ear pain; no neck stiffness at present (neck stiffness listed as red flag to report if develops).
- Relevant past episodes and treatments:
  - No prior history of headaches of this type.
  - Family history: mother has migraines.
  - No prior hospital care, ED visits, or injection therapy mentioned.
- Allergies and current medications:
  - Allergies: patient states none.
  - Current/recent medications: Nurofen (ibuprofen) taken yesterday — dose/route/frequency not documented.
  - Regular medications: none.
- Relevant social context:
  - Lives with partner.
  - Occupation: designer; currently finding it difficult to do normal work.
  - Non-smoker, no alcohol use reported, no recreational drugs.

Objective:
- Observable swelling and distribution: none reported.
- Airway/breathing descriptors: no stridor or work-of-breathing concerns reported.
- Mental status and associated features: alert, oriented, communicating appropriately; no dizziness or syncope reported.
- Vitals and examination findings: Not recorded.
- Presence of another person with the patient: No other person reported present during the consultation; patient reports living with a partner.

Assessment:
- Clinical impression:
  - Acute primary headache of new onset, severe (8/10), localized left posterior head; features not suggestive of systemic infection or focal neurological deficit based on history.
- Key justifications from transcript:
  - Rapid onset yesterday, intense throbbing pain, no nausea/vomiting, no visual changes, no fever, no rash, no neurologic symptoms reported.
- Conflict noted:
  - None identified.

Plan:
- Immediate actions taken/advised:
  - Trial of stronger analgesia recommended (specific agent not documented) to be taken instead of ibuprofen; advised to take regularly with food.
  - Paracetamol advised as an adjunct and may be taken alongside the recommended analgesic.
  - Rest and maintain good hydration.
- Specific instructions provided to patient:
  - If pain worsens, or new symptoms develop (fever, rash, vomiting, neck stiffness), contact the service.
  - If headaches persist or repeat, contact the service to discuss further management.
  - Advised to try the recommended medication regimen from pharmacy and re-contact if not improving.
- Escalation criteria / red flags:
  - Worsening pain, development of fever, rash, vomiting, neck stiffness, new neurological signs, or recurrent similar episodes.
- Follow-up:
  - Return contact/call back if symptoms not settling within the next day or two after trying recommended medications; further assessment and planning will be arranged as needed.
- COVID-19 vaccine suitability:
  - Not discussed.
- Emergency contact instructions as stated:
  - "Give us a call back" if symptoms worsen or do not settle after trying medication; contact if new symptoms (fever, rash, vomiting, neck stiffness) occur.

Quality checks (document_quality):
- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - Vital signs (BP, pulse, respiratory rate, temperature).
  - Focused neurological examination (cranial nerves, motor/sensory, coordination).
  - Head and neck examination (inspection/palpation for focal signs).
  - Specific name/dose/route/frequency of the "stronger analgesic" recommended.
  - Documentation of analgesic effectiveness beyond initial ibuprofen attempt.
  - Formal migraine-specific history (aura, photophobia, phonophobia) beyond brief denial of visual disturbance.
  - Formal redirection to emergency services if severe new focal deficits develop.
- Internal conflicts from the transcript:
  - None identified.
- Transcript quality:
  - Audio transcript appears clear and complete; no significant inaudible segments noted.
